hops.query: tariff impact on product cost gross margin
hops.rationale: Passages from ISRG's 2026 filing (Item 7) together cover the requested goal, tariff impacts on product cost. Passage 7 states tariffs are expected to adversely affect the product cost of the da Vinci Xi system in China, that pass-through supplier tariffs were incurred, and that tariffs and trade measures raised cost of revenues by about $63.0 million in 2025 with further increases expected in 2026. Passage 42 says product gross profit margin fell in 2025 primarily due to new tariffs, and passage 43 says service gross margin also fell partly due to new tariffs. Passages 6 and 8 add the sourcing context (Mexico/USMCA, German endoscopes, Chinese imports) and the forward-looking tariff risk. No required element within the ISRG 2026 Item 7 scope is missing. The da Vinci procedure growth topic is outside this subquery and was not graded.

hops.query: da Vinci procedure growth systems installed base procedures
hops.rationale: Within ISRG's Item 7 scope, the passages directly address da Vinci procedure growth: utilization per system up 3% in 2025, installed base of about 11,106 systems (up 12%), 1,721 placements (up 13%), and OUS gynecology procedure growth of about 28% in 2025 versus 29% in 2024, with urology growth discussed. Ion procedure growth (about 144,100 vs 95,500) is also covered, though it is outside the da Vinci goal. The headline company-wide da Vinci procedure volume growth percentage for 2025 and the U.S. procedure growth split are not visible; the passage at the start of the urology discussion is cut off and the text before passage 19 is missing. Score is 4 because the core growth disclosures are present, with that headline figure as the gap.

The growth in hysterectomy procedures has been largely driven by increased use of our systems by new da Vinci surgeons. Ion Procedures The adoption of robotic-assisted bronchoscopy using the Ion endoluminal system has the potential to grow if it can offer greater patient value than non-Ion alternatives and competitive total economics for healthcare providers. The increase in our overall procedure volume in 2025 reflects a larger installed base of approximately 995 systems, an increase of 24% compared to the installed base of approximately 805 systems as of 2024. In 2025, tariffs and other trade measures have increased our cost of revenues by approximately $63.0 million. Based on the announced and implemented global tariffs as of the date of this report, and assuming such tariffs remain in place, we expect our cost of revenues driven by tariffs and other trade measures to continue to increase in 2026.

Product gross profit margin decreased in 2025 compared to 2024, primarily driven by new tariffs, incremental fixed overhead costs, including depreciation expense associated with expanded manufacturing capacity, and higher costs associated with our da Vinci 5 surgical system, partially offset by lower excess and obsolete inventory charges.
We also import certain raw materials and finished goods from outside of the U.S. that are subject to tariffs, including our endoscopes, a majority of which are manufactured in Germany.
1,721 da Vinci surgical systems were placed during the year ended December 31, 2025, an increase of 13% compared to 1,526 systems during the year ended December 31, 2024.
Utilization of da Vinci surgical systems, measured in terms of procedures per system per year, increased 3% relative to 2024.
OUS gynecology procedures grew approximately 28% in 2025, compared to approximately 29% in 2024, most notably hysterectomy procedures.

The adoption of robotic-assisted surgery using the da Vinci surgical system has the potential to grow for those procedures that offer greater patient value than to non-da Vinci alternatives and competitive total economics for healthcare providers.
